title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood in Austin, Texas. The vehicle had a human safety operator on board but did not slow down or stop before hitting the animal. This shows a failure in the system's object detection or decision-making when encountering an obstacle in its path, occurring during normal deployment in a populated area.

The incident was not caught before deployment because the vehicle was already operating with passengers in the neighborhood. It would have required either better obstacle detection in the autonomous system itself, or a safety operator prepared to intervene. The operator's presence did not prevent the collision.

Whether the autonomous system failed to perceive the duck, perceived it but did not classify it as an obstacle requiring avoidance, or made some other error is not established by the reports.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern about self-driving cars in residential areas. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which had a human safety operator on board, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was well-known to residents because it nested in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant. After a neighborhood resident posted about the incident on Facebook, local media coverage drew attention to the accident and raised questions about autonomous vehicle safety and whether they should operate in populated neighborhoods.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the claim that it failed to stop at a stop sign, finding no evidence to support that assertion. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations in the future. Meanwhile, concerned residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Other companies including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate autonomous vehicles in Austin.
